rendered.overview: This Non-black deck is a five-color Ally and Lesson pile led by [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]]. Airbend, earthbend and firebend effects draw cards off the commander, who then transforms to drain each opponent. [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] together also make infinite creature triggers as a backup.

strategy: Ramp with [[Bender's Waterskin]] and [[Earthbender Ascension]] to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Earthbend with [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] and [[Earthbending Lesson]] so each bend draws a card.
Airbend with [[Airbending Lesson]] and [[Glider Staff]], then attack to firebend and finish all four types in one turn.
Transform the commander at upkeep to draw four cards and deal 4 damage to each opponent.
Backup: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] and [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] with the commander loop enter and leave triggers.

keep: [[Hermitic Herbalist]] or [[Bender's Waterskin]] with a bending spell starts the engine.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] plus cheap Lessons keeps the bending going.
sendBack: Expensive [[Water Whip]] and [[Crashing Wave]] with no early mana stall out.
Hands missing most of the five colors cannot cast the bending spells.

cards: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
tips.text: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] airbends your permanents, then casting them from exile creates Ally tokens and triggers [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]].
[[Katara, the Fearless]] doubles triggers of Allies like [[Haru, Hidden Talent]], so each Ally entering earthbends twice.
[[Uncle Iroh]] makes Lessons cheaper, and [[Gran-Gran]] gets cheaper noncreature spells once three Lessons are in the graveyard.

weaknesses: Moderate: Removal like [[Swords to Plowshares]] on [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] stops the card draw and the drain plan.
Minor: Lesson payoffs like [[Gran-Gran]] want three Lessons in the graveyard, so [[Bojuka Bog]] shuts that off.
Minor: [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] dying to removal like [[Swords to Plowshares]] breaks the backup loop.

rendered.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifact deck that proliferates every time it taps. Mana rocks and artifact lands feed a pile of counter sources, [[Lux Artillery]] and [[Dragonspark Reactor]] turn them into damage, and several small combos are on hand.

strategy: Ramp with rocks and artifact lands, then cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3.
Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] each turn, using its haste, to proliferate counters on artifacts and creatures.
Add proliferate sources like [[Surge Conductor]] and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] to multiply the counters.
Finish with [[Lux Artillery]] at thirty counters or with [[Dragonspark Reactor]] damage.
Backup: [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Steel Overseer]] and [[Crystalline Crawler]] makes infinite counters.

keep: [[Surge Conductor]] plus cheap rocks starts the counter engine.
[[Thought Monitor]] with artifacts in hand refills it.
sendBack: Only expensive artifacts and no white or blue source.
Lands with no artifacts to feed the engine.

tips.text: [[Surge Conductor]] proliferates whenever a nontoken artifact enters, so cast rocks after [[Lux Artillery]] to build counters.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles each proliferate, so [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] taps add two counters.
[[Pemmin's Aura]] on [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] untaps it for blue mana, proliferating each time with [[Relic of Legends]].

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever it becomes tapped.
Proliferates when other artifacts enter.
Doubles every proliferate you do.
Deals 10 to each opponent at thirty counters.
Untaps a creature for repeated triggers.
Adds counters to artifact creatures.
Pairs with auras for looting loops.

weaknesses: Critical: A deck made of artifacts is exposed to [[Vandalblast]] or [[Collector Ouphe]], with only [[Lux Cannon]] and [[Chaos Warp]] to answer.
Moderate: Without [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] the deck leans on [[Surge Conductor]] and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]], which an opposing [[Swords to Plowshares]] can remove.
Minor: Many tapped lands and painlands slow development, and three colors with few basics can stumble against [[Blood Moon]].

plans.primary: Build a pile of artifacts and counters, then use [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and other proliferate sources to grow counters until [[Lux Artillery]] hits for 10 or a swollen creature finishes the game.
backups: Assemble [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] for infinite draw and looting, or with [[Steel Overseer]] and [[Crystalline Crawler]] for infinite counters.
Use [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] to take infinite extra turns.

rendered.overview: This colorless Eldrazi and artifact ramp deck piles up mana from rocks and utility lands, then casts [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] around turn 5 so its big colorless spells cascade twice. It wins through annihilator Eldrazi, artifact creatures, planeswalkers, and [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana.

strategy: Open with [[Sol Ring]], [[Thran Dynamo]] and [[Palladium Myr]] to reach six mana quickly.
Cast [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]], then follow with colorless spells of mana value 7 or more to cascade twice each.
Land [[Artisan of Kozilek]] and [[It That Betrays]] and attack with annihilator to strip the opposing boards.
Use [[Ugin, the Spirit Dragon]] or [[Perilous Vault]] to clear colored permanents when behind.
Backup: [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] make infinite colorless mana.

keep: [[Thran Dynamo]] or [[Palladium Myr]] on a hand with lands starts the ramp.
[[Eye of Ugin]] with an Eldrazi to cast cheaply.
sendBack: Hands of only expensive Eldrazi with no early mana source.
Hands with only [[Basalt Monolith]] and no way to ramp.

tips.text: [[Ugin, the Ineffable]] makes colorless spells cost two less, helping reach mana value 7 for [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] triggers.
[[Darksteel Monolith]] lets you cast a colorless spell for zero from hand, which can still be a cascade source with [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]].
[[Basalt Monolith]] untaps for three, and [[Manifold Key]] can untap it for one.

rendered.overview: Naya Dinosaur deck led by [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]]. Mana creatures and cost reducers like [[Knight of the Stampede]] get big trampling Dinosaurs out fast. Then the team attacks, and each connection with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] drops more Dinosaurs onto the battlefield. Enrage creatures and sweepers add a second route.

strategy: Ramp with [[Atzocan Seer]] and [[Topiary Stomper]], and cut costs with [[Knight of the Stampede]].
Connect with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to put revealed Dinosaurs onto the battlefield.
[[Garruk's Uprising]] gives trample and draws cards, while [[Annoyed Altisaur]] cascades into more threats.
Alternate win: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] make infinite tokens and damage to all creatures.
Backup: [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Walking Ballista]] make infinite +1/+1 counters.

keep: [[Atzocan Seer]] into a cheap Dinosaur starts the engine.
[[Knight of the Stampede]] alongside Dinosaurs to cast.
sendBack: Big Dinosaurs with no early ramp to cast them.
Red or white cards with no source for those colors.

tips.text: [[Fiery Confluence]] damages each creature, which triggers the enrage on [[Ripjaw Raptor]] and draws a card.
[[Forerunner of the Empire]] pings every creature when a Dinosaur enters, triggering enrage on [[Trapjaw Tyrant]].
[[Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma]] makes power 4 or greater creatures cheaper, so [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]] costs even less.

rendered.overview: Mono-red Goblins deck in Red. [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] doubles the Goblin count each turn while cheap Goblins, [[Dragon Fodder]] and [[Mogg War Marshal]] fill the board. It wins by swinging wide with haste and pump, or with [[Skirk Prospector]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Goblin Warchief]] for an infinite loop.

strategy: Cast cheap Goblins and token makers like [[Dragon Fodder]] and [[Mogg War Marshal]] to grow the Goblin count.
Land [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 and tap it each turn to double the Goblins.
Give the board haste with [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]], then swing wide and pump with [[Goblin Lookout]].
Alternate win: [[Skirk Prospector]], [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Goblin Warchief]] make infinite tokens and death triggers.
Finish with burn like [[Fireball]] or [[Goblin Grenade]] when blockers stall the attack.

keep: [[Mogg War Marshal]] or [[Dragon Fodder]] with red mana starts the Goblin count.
[[Goblin Matron]] fetches a Goblin to fill the curve.
sendBack: Expensive spells and no cheap Goblins to build a board.
Only pump and burn with no Goblins to use them.

tips.text: [[Goblin Warchief]] gives Goblins haste, so tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] can attack the turn they arrive.
[[Goblin Bombardment]] sacrifices tokens from [[Mogg War Marshal]] for damage, and the Marshal leaves another token when it dies.
[[Pashalik Mons]] pings whenever a Goblin dies, so sacrificing to [[Tar Pitcher]] adds extra damage.

keyCards.job: Doubles the Goblin count each turn.
Hands Goblins haste and cheaper spells.
Pumps Goblins and gives them haste.
Sacrifice outlet that turns Goblins into mana.
Fetches a key Goblin on entry.
Makes two bodies for the Goblin count.
Pings on each Goblin death.
Turns tokens into reach damage.

weaknesses: Moderate: Removal on [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] such as [[Swords to Plowshares]] stops the doubling, and the deck then relies on smaller Goblins.
Moderate: Most wins are combat attacks, so [[Settle the Wreckage]] or [[Propaganda]] can stall the wide board.
Minor: Nothing here answers an opposing enchantment such as [[Propaganda]], though artifacts are covered.

backups: Assemble [[Skirk Prospector]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and either [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] for infinite commander casts, hasty tokens and death triggers.
Burn out opponents with [[Fireball]], [[Volcanic Geyser]] and [[Goblin Grenade]], backed by [[Guttersnipe]].

rendered.overview: Jeskai partner deck led by [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]. Attacking with Gods and Gods dying build experience counters, which become +1/+1 counters and cards. Proliferate pieces and [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] press the damage, with extra combats as a backup.

strategy: Ramp into [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] around turn 4, using talismans and [[Solemn Simulacrum]].
Attack with Gods such as [[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] to earn experience counters, which [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] turns into +1/+1 counters.
Use [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to draw per experience counter and deal 2 damage to each opponent.
Proliferate with [[Flux Channeler]] and [[Inexorable Tide]] to grow experience counters and counters on creatures.
Backup: [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] add combats so [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] makes more Rebels.

keep: [[Talisman of Progress]] plus a God to attack with.
[[Solemn Simulacrum]] and a way to draw into Gods.
sendBack: Only red or only blue lands with no way to cast the white spells.
Expensive [[Aggravated Assault]] with no early plays.

tips.text: [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds an extra counter whenever you would put counters on yourself, so each experience gain from [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] counts for more.

cards: Toralf, God of Fury // Toralf's Hammer
tips.text: [[Surtr, Fiery Jötun]] deals 3 damage on each historic spell, and [[Toralf, God of Fury]] copies excess noncombat damage to another target.
[[All Will Be One]] deals damage for each counter placed, so [[Inexorable Tide]] proliferating on every spell hits an opponent.

keyCards.job: Earns experience and grows a creature each end step.
Turns experience into cards and damage.
Attacks for growing Rebel token waves.
Boosts every counter you put on yourself.
Proliferates on every spell you cast.
Converts counter placement into damage.
Makes hasty fliers from each card drawn.
Pings opponents when creatures enter.

weaknesses: Moderate: Many enchantment Gods and counter engines fall to [[Vandalblast]] or [[Farewell]], and the deck has only [[Chaos Warp]] to answer opposing ones.
Moderate: Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], experience counters stop growing, so repeated removal or a [[Rest in Peace]]-style tax slows the plan.
Moderate: Wins lean on combat, so [[Propaganda]] or a fog-style effect stalls most attacks.

Proliferate with [[Flux Channeler]] and [[Inexorable Tide]] to grow experience counters and counters on creatures.
Backup: [[Aggravated Assault]] and [[World at War]] add combats so [[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] makes more Rebels.

tips.text: [[Lae'zel, Vlaakith's Champion]] adds an extra counter whenever you would put counters on yourself, so each experience gain from [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] counts for more.

[[All Will Be One]] deals damage for each counter placed, so [[Inexorable Tide]] proliferating on every spell hits an opponent.

Turns experience into cards and damage.
Attacks for growing Rebel token waves.

assessment.line: Many enchantment Gods and counter engines fall to [[Vandalblast]] or [[Farewell]], and the deck has only [[Chaos Warp]] to answer opposing ones.
Only 3 of 9 interaction pieces are cheap instants, so a fast combo from an opponent is hard to stop in time.
Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]], experience counters stop growing, so repeated removal or a [[Rest in Peace]]-style tax slows the plan.
Wins lean on combat, so [[Propaganda]] or a fog-style effect stalls most attacks.
Three colors with many tapped or conditional lands and pain lands can leave white or blue short early.

rendered.overview: This Mono-Blue Wizards deck runs a wall of counterspells and cheap cantrips on top of [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]], who makes them cheaper and loots on every counter. It wins by flashing in [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to loop with [[Sublime Epiphany]] or [[Ghostly Flicker]], or by decking itself for [[Laboratory Maniac]].

strategy: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 so counters and cantrips cost less.
Counter threats with [[Counterspell]] and [[Mana Leak]], looting off each counter with Baral.
Dig with [[Brainstorm]] and [[Preordain]] to find [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] and a spell to copy.
Flash in [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] on the stack to start the loop.
Backup: draw out the library, then [[Laboratory Maniac]] or [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]] wins on the next draw.

keep: [[Preordain]] or [[Brainstorm]] with a cheap counter keeps the engine going.
[[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] alongside an instant to copy.
sendBack: Expensive wizards and no counter or cantrip to interact early.
Only reactive counters with no way to dig toward [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]].

tips.text: [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] copies [[Sublime Epiphany]] on entering, and the loop needs 4 mana.
[[Ghostly Flicker]] can blink [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to copy itself again, with 7 mana needed.
[[Archmage of Runes]] draws on each spell, and [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] makes those spells cheaper.
[[Sea Gate Stormcaller]] copies a cheap cantrip like [[Preordain]] when it enters.

Flexible instant that powers the loop.
Blinks Naru Meha for repeated copies.

Mills you out and wins on empty draw.

weaknesses: Moderate: Wins hinge on [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] or a self-mill, so a counter on it or a [[Stifle]] effect stalls the plan.
Moderate: Removal on [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] in response to its trigger breaks both loops.
Minor: Blue has no way to answer an opposing [[Rest in Peace]] or similar enchantment except bouncing it with [[Sublime Epiphany]].

rendered.overview: This Dimir deck is built around Ninjas. Cheap unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] connect, then ninjutsu swaps in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or another Ninja. Each hit draws cards and drains life, while counterspells protect the attack. Extra-turn spells add more combat steps.

strategy: Cast cheap unblockable creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Triton Shorestalker]] to start attacking.
Once a creature is unblocked, ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] to trigger damage effects.
Each Ninja hit makes [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] reveal a card, draw it and drain opponents for its mana value.
Hold [[Counterspell]] and [[Negate]] mana to protect the attack, and rebuy attackers with ninjutsu returns.
Alternate win: [[Temporal Manipulation]] or [[Time Warp]] gives extra turns for more attacks.

keep: [[Slither Blade]] with a cheap Ninja gives an early ninjutsu line.
[[Mistblade Shinobi]] plus an unblockable attacker starts the chain.
sendBack: Expensive spells with no unblockable creature to attack with.
Only one color of mana when the hand needs both blue and black.

tips.text: [[Silver-Fur Master]] makes ninjutsu cheaper and pumps Ninjas, so [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] drains more.
[[Ingenious Infiltrator]] draws a card on every Ninja hit, adding to [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] triggers.

keyCards.job: Cheap ninjutsu that draws on a hit.
Tutors Ninjas and grants unblockability.
Discounts ninjutsu and pumps Ninjas.
Gives creatures in hand ninjutsu.
Unblockable attacker to enable ninjutsu.
Extra turn for more attacks.
Protects the attack from spells.

weaknesses: Moderate: Combat-based plan can be shut down by [[Propaganda]] or a sweeper like [[Toxic Deluge]] that clears small attackers.
